title: Phases, metrics, and techniques of product discovery
organization_or_sample: Online articles, blogs, reports, and books
method: Review and synthesis of gray literature
search_query: product discovery product management customer research agile
key_finding: Organizes discovery practices into phases, metrics, and techniques; the abstract says the review draws on gray literature and calls for peer-reviewed research.
time_savings_evidence: No quantified hours reported in abstract.
quality_outcome_evidence: Authors suggest better discovery may support user-centric products and satisfaction; this is not a causal estimate.
evidence_limitations: Not empirical validation of PO needs; gray-literature base; no bank comparator.
screening_note: Use as a map of practice vocabulary, not as evidence of prevalence or impact.

title: Toward an Agile Product Management: What Do Product Managers Do in Agile Companies?
source_type: Peer-reviewed book chapter / multiple case study
organization_or_sample: 17 interviews with 11 product managers in four agile companies
method: Multiple case study; semi-structured interviews per abstract
search_query: product discovery product management customer research agile
linked_hypothesis: Time and structured practice; customer perspective
key_finding: Reports continuous product experimentation and innovation, team support, and additional product-management activities.
time_savings_evidence: No measured time savings reported in abstract.
quality_outcome_evidence: No direct profitability or usability outcome reported in abstract.
evidence_limitations: PMs rather than novice POs; non-banking sample; abstract does not quantify task time or discovery quality.
screening_note: Relevant to role activities, not a direct test of the BP hypotheses.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Management: The Automation-Augmentation Paradox
organization_or_sample: Management domain; three business books used as starting point
method: Paradox-theory argument; not an empirical intervention study
search_query: artificial intelligence product discovery usability customer research product management
key_finding: Argues automation and augmentation are interdependent and that overemphasizing either can create negative outcomes; recommends considering both together.
quality_outcome_evidence: No profitability or usability outcomes measured.
evidence_limitations: Normative conceptual reasoning based on a limited set of books; no evidence specific to product discovery or banking.
screening_note: Use to frame a human-oversight question, not to claim that AI improves quality.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Lean Startup Method, and Product Innovations
method: Abstract reports analysis of startup data and policy shifts encouraging AI adoption
search_query: artificial intelligence product discovery usability customer research product management
key_finding: The abstract reports complementarity between AI and Lean Startup methods for product innovation, with discovery-oriented AI expanding market-opportunity search and controlled experimentation helping validate opportunities.
time_savings_evidence: Abstract reports higher-quality products in less time, but not a four-hour saving or PO-task-level measurement.
quality_outcome_evidence: Product quality is discussed; customer usability and bank profitability are not established in the abstract.
evidence_limitations: Chinese startups, not banks; full-text operationalization and causal design not reviewed; not a direct measure of PO effort.
screening_note: Promising adjacent evidence for AI-plus-experimentation; transferability is limited.
